answer: One defense is stake-bonded identity: before an agent can transact, it locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if it cheats. A single honest agent pays once, but a Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so forging ten thousand clones costs ten thousand deposits plus the opportunity cost of locked capital. Like a glacier advancing grain by grain, the bond makes mass forgery slow and expensive, while a wharf-style checkpoint verifying the bond before granting port access and a dune of reputation that only grows through honest trades keep cheap throwaway identities out.
